problem:
Given that
$B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $B=LU,$ then ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=$
worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $B$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $B$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot B \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-0.25){R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -0.25 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot B \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}B=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}B & =U \\ {E}_{1}B & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ B & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ B & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -0.25 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ B & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.25 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ B & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.25 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{32}=0.25,{u}_{33}=-3,$ and ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=-0.75.$
